claim: Let \(\mathcal T\) be the class of finite simple connected graphs of diameter at most \(2\) that admit maps \(f_1,f_2\) satisfying Tajima--Yoshinaga Definition 5.1, and let \(\mathcal P\) be the pawful graphs. Up to isomorphism, \(\mathcal T\setminus\mathcal P\) has no graph on at most \(5\) vertices and exactly one graph on \(6\) vertices, namely Tajima--Yoshinaga's graph \(G_1\). Equivalently, their sufficient condition first strictly enlarges the pawful class at order \(6\), uniquely. The counts \((|\mathcal P_n|,|\mathcal T_n|)\) for \(n=1,\ldots,6\) are \((1,1),(1,1),(2,2),(5,5),(13,13),(47,48)\).

correctness.rationale: The standard-library verifier exhausts every graph-isomorphism orbit through six vertices, proves complete coverage of all labeled graphs, implements the Definition 5.1 existential constraints exactly, and replays the published G1 f1/f2 witness. The resulting strict-extension counts are 0 through order 5 and exactly 1 at order 6.

value.rationale: The paper proposes Definition 5.1 as a genuine extension of pawfulness. Determining exactly when that extension first becomes strict, and whether the first witness is unique, is a natural sharpness question. The exhaustive result shows equality through order five and a unique strict class at order six, while preserving the important distinction from all diagonal graphs.
